English: When he came to the stairs, it happened that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;

Limbum: Kúr beèe ca a m ce duè a yeâ mbuèu a ce ghaa a ce laèa enáê, “Yú neè ye!”
English: for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, Away with him!

Limbum: A ka' koo Pol tá a bo niñ aègho mbe barakïì, e laa neè ñwáè ce e m ba tu bsoogáè yïû goèr ca naè enáê, “AÈde' m laa yuu a?” E beesïì enáê, “Baná wáâ ke laèa li Greâk a?
English: As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he asked the commanding officer, May I speak to you? He said, Do you know Greek?

Limbum: Mboè a wáè ñwáâ aè to' Ijïìp ce e m káè' ñgá', a lor ñgaâa nyúshi beèe ncúèkïì kyeèe aè nfeè' moè' a du aègho aè ntee rïìñ naè a?”
English: Aren't you then the Egyptian, who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?

Limbum: Pol aè beesïì enáê, “M yu ñwáè Jus ce aè rla' Tasoâs aè ñgoâñ Sïìlesïìyaè ce yu rla' ce li yu aètáèr ka'. Kyer wáè, maè'shi tá m laa yuu neè beèe ca.”
English: But Paul said, I am a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.

Limbum: Ñwáè anaè aè ma'shïì ená e laêa. Pol aè táá mbe dïì' ce e m ko' a táá naè, a naa bo mbekïì ená beèe a cu nyañ. Beèe a ka' cu nyañ, e laa neè woweèe aè li Hibruè enáê,
English: When he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand to the people. When there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,

Limbum: “Yaè beèe, bfúr waê, ba yaè ta weèe, yu' neè yuu ce e m be laèa.”
English: Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make to you.

Limbum: Woweèe a ka' yu' aèmboè e laèa neè woweèe ba aè li Hibruè, woweèe a misïì a cu nyoèñ. Pol aè laa enáê,
English: When they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they were even more quiet. He said,

Limbum: “M yu ñwáè Jus ce a m bi ba aè rla' Tasoès aè ñgoâñ Sïìlesïìyaè. Geewa'a, máè m kuè' aè rlaâ' aèfa na. Máè m cu njeptii Gaèmalïìyaèl, e yá'nïì máè mncir viseèe btarkú boèñboñ seê, ya ntee yi ce luèu máè aè rduè aèmbuèu Nyúè aèmboè ye foñ yi ce luèu ntïìni na.”
English: I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict tradition of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as you all are this day.

Limbum: Máè laa mánáê, ‘M be geèe má ká Tataê?’ Tata aè beesïì enáê, ‘Naèti mbekïì du aè rla' Daèmaskoès. AÈ be baè' aèfo tá a suñ wáè buu wááwá ce Taèr aè ce ená aè geêe.’
English: I said, 'What shall I do, Lord?' The Lord said to me, 'Arise, and go into Damascus. There you will be told about all things which are appointed for you to do.'

Limbum: Rraa ce li m raa naè li m niñ máè njep mmïìr, máè feêp, beèe ce weèr woweèe aè m ba a koo máè aè boè a du aègho aè rla' Daèmaskoès.
English: When I couldn't see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.

Limbum: “Ñwáè moè' ce a m ce too ená AÈnaèniyaès aè m ba aè rla' anaè, aè ba ñwáè ce e m ce láè mncir yáánïì seê. Jus aèfo wááwá a m ce laèa boèñboñ aèmboè ye seê.
English: One Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus,

Limbum: E m vúè a yá máè, a táá a máâ geñ a laa enáê, ‘Nfúraâ Soêl, yá buu.’ Máè yá buu aè nfeè' anaè, a yá ye aèmboè e táá.
English: came to me, and standing by me said to me, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight!' In that very hour I looked up at him.

Limbum: E laa enáê, ‘Nyúè yïì viseèe btarkú aè ce wáè tá aè bo rïìñ yuu ce e ce koèñ ená aè geêe, keèr yá yïì Ñwáè Rfaâ' Nyáánïì, yu' aèmboè e ce laèa,
English: He said, 'The God of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.

Limbum: njobeè' aè be ba yïì ñwáè ce aè be suñ beèe wááwá buu ce wáè yá a ker yu'.
English: For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.

Limbum: AÈ ker ce keè' ba ká seè'ni? Naèti mbekïì, ká' li rlii, tá a baptir wáè, suè'si yoè buu bebep.’
English: Now why do you wait? Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.'

Limbum: “Máè ka' kúti aè rla' Jáèrusaláèm ce geèe rloo mbe Ndaèp Nyúè, a yá njáèá rlo mo'.
English: It happened that, when I had returned to Jerusalem, and while I prayed in the temple, I fell into a trance,

Limbum: Pol aè m ce laèa beèe a ku ce yu'shi, e ka' ce laèa aèmboè beèe enje jáá, woweèe a ghaêa, a laa enáê, “Weèe fa maè'shi ye ka', yú neè ye.”
English: They listened to him until he said that; then they lifted up their voice, and said, Rid the earth of this fellow, for he isn't fit to live!

Limbum: Woweèe a ce ghaa, a co'ni wap bcáè' a ce maè'ri, ce dú'si nfúènfú mbekïì.
English: As they cried out, and threw off their cloaks, and threw dust into the air,

Limbum: Ñwáè ce e m ba tu naè aè laa ená a lor Pol niñ aègho mbe barakïì, lip ye, bipshi buu neè ye tá a bo rïìñ mbuèu ce Jus a m ce ghaa ye aè njáâá wa'a.
English: the commanding officer commanded him to be brought into the barracks, ordering him to be examined by scourging, that he might know for what crime they shouted against him like that.

Limbum: Woweèe a kur ye tá a bo lïìp, e laa neè ñwáè ce e m ba tu neè bsoogáè rjeèe enáê, “Waè' ncir yi byemi ená a lip ñwáè Rum ce a be sa' yïì nsa' ka' a?”
English: When they had tied him up with thongs, Paul asked the centurion who stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and not found guilty?

Limbum: Ñwáè ce e m ba tu neè bsoogáè rjeèe naè aè ka' yu' ca, a du a suñ neè tu yïû goèr. E m laèa neè ye enáê, “AÈ be geèe wáká seè'ni aè? Ñwáè ca yu ñwáè Ruêm.”
English: When the centurion heard it, he went to the commanding officer and told him, Watch what you are about to do, for this man is a Roman!

Limbum: Tu yïû goèr yi du a yá Poêl, a bipshi neè ye enáê, “Suñ ka máè láê, aè yu ñwáè Rum a?” E beesïì ená áèno.
English: The commanding officer came and asked him, Tell me, are you a Roman? He said, Yes.

Limbum: Tu ca yi laa neè ye enáê, “Máè m laè' ku' mbaèa goèr seê, ka' ba ñwáè Ruêm.” Pol aè laa enáê, “A m bi yi máè aè ñwáè Ruêm.”
English: The commanding officer answered, I bought my citizenship for a great price. Paul said, But I was born a Roman.

Limbum: Beèe ce a m ba ená a be bipshi buu neè ye naè, a natïì a táá encaèñ. Tu yïû goèr foñ yi m loè a wáp aè nfeè' ce e m rïìñ ená e koo Pol ce yu ñwáè Ruêm, a kur.
English: Immediately those who were about to examine him departed from him, and the commanding officer also was afraid when he realized that he was a Roman, because he had bound him.

Limbum: Tu yïû goèr yi m ce koèñ aè rrïìñ rara ená Jus ca a m ce laèa ená Pol aè geèe ba ká lá. Túè' aè ka' raa, e ba'shïì ye efa bshañ, a laa beâe bgoèrgoèr efa múè ñgaâa tañshi tañshïì ba ñgaâa kansuèr wááwá a vúseè. E vú neè Pol a tár mbe kansuèr.
English: But on the next day, desiring to know the truth about why he was accused by the Jews, he freed him from the bonds, and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.

Limbum: Pol aè fyá' ñgaâa kansuèr ená ntuñ-ñ-ñ, a laa enáê, “Yaè beèe, máè cu la rcu vú ba' ntïìni na neè ntee rara-ñwáè aè bsii Nyúè.”
English: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until this day.

Limbum: Tu ñgaâa tañshi tañshïì ce a n ce too ená AÈnaèniyaès aè laa neè beèe ce a m táá aègee Pol ená woweèe a lip ye aè cuèu.
English: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.

Limbum: Pol aè laa neè ye enáê, “Nyúè be lïìp wáè, wáè ce aè yu aèmboè ñgúè' ndap mbúú. Wáè loèr mncir a ce sa' máè aègho, a ker ce bú' mncir anaè njobeè' wáè laèa ená a lip máè.”
English: Then Paul said to him, God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?

Limbum: Beèe ce a m táá aègee Pol, a laa neè ye enáê, “AÈ ce cáp tu ñgaâa tañshi tañshïì yïû Nyúè a?”
English: Those who stood by said, Do you malign God's high priest?

Limbum: Pol aè beesïì enáê, “Bfúr waê, máè ba riñ ená a tu ñgaâa tañshi tañshïì ka'. A sañ mbe Ñwaâ' Nyúè enáê, ‘Fa laèa yuu bebep kuèu ñwáè ce e ce sa' yoè beèe ka'.’ ”
English: Paul said, I didn't know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, 'You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.'

Limbum: Pol aè m rïìñ ená beèe mo' embe kansuèr a yu Saduèsïî, beèe mo' a ba Farïìsïî, a laa neè ñgaâa kansuèr enáê, “Yaè beèe, m yu ñwáè Farïìsïî, a ba muu ñwáè Farïìsïî. M táá mbe kansuèr na aè mnsa' njo' m ce keè' ená beèe ce a kweñger a be keè fúú efa rkwe.”
English: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!

Limbum: E ka' laèa wa'a, beèe Farïìsi ba beèe Saduèsï a ká' a ce lapni, a fúú nto' baa.
English: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.

Limbum: Beèe Saduèsi a kani ená nfúú-efa-rkwe yu aègho ka', a ker kani ená bcïìndap Nyúè ker ba byú' vi yu aègho ka'. Beèe Farïìsi a byemïì ená buu ca wááwá yu aègho.
English: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.

Limbum: Beèe a misïì a ghaa goèr seê, beèe mo' efa ñgaâa ryá'ni mncir ce a m ba yap beèe Farïìsïî, a natïì mbekïì a laa tatap seê, enáê, Weèr a yá faèa moè' neè ñwáè ca ka'! Seèe rïìñ neè ká aèmboè aè laèa ba yú' mo' káè ncïìndap Nyúè neè ye.
English: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees part stood up, and contended, saying, We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let's not fight against God!

Limbum: Beèe a lapnïì goèr seê, tu yïû goèr yi wáp ená a be koo Pol saèsi. E laa neè bsoogáè ená woweèe a du koo ye aè ñger niñ aègho mbe barakïì.
English: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them, and bring him into the barracks.

Limbum: Túè' aè ka' sii, Tata Jisoès aè vú a táá aègee Poêl, a laa neè ye enáê, “Táá tatap, fa wáp ka'! Wáè suñ beèe aèmboè máè aè rla' Jáèrusaláèm, aè be duè suñ beèe aèmboè máè foñ aè rla' Ruêm.”
English: The following night, the Lord stood by him, and said, Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.

Limbum: Túè' aè ka' raa, Jus mo' a cuteè a ye leè' ená woweèe a ka' tá yú Pol ka' woweèe a ye yuu ka', ker no yuu ka'.
English: When it was day, some of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

Limbum: Beèe ce a m ye leè' ca a m caèa beèe mkyeèe.
English: There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.

Limbum: Woweèe a du a yá beâe bgoèrgoèr efa múè ñgaâa tañshi tañshïì ba bleebeèe, a laa neè woweèe enáê, “Weèr aè ye leè' tatap seê, ená weèr aè ka' tá yú Pol ka' weèr joo yuu kuè cuèu ka'.
English: They came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.

Limbum: Baná weèe kansuèr weèe aè ba cep ntuu neè tu yïû goèr ená e vú neè Pol fa neè weèe, aèmboè weèe ce lá koèñ aè rfyá' njep múè vi mnsa' boèñboñ wa'a. Weèr aè tami nyor aè ryú ye tá e ka' vúè baè'.”
English: Now therefore, you with the council inform the commanding officer that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to judge his case more exactly. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.

Limbum: Muu njar Pol aè yu' mncúè ce woweèe a m cúè na, a du a niñ mbe barakïì a suñ Poêl.
English: But Paul's sister's son heard of their lying in wait, and he came and entered into the barracks and told Paul.

Limbum: Pol aè ká' tu mo', a laa neè ye enáê, “Loèr muu nsuènsuè ca du fa neè tu yïû goèr, e roèo suñ ye yuu mo'.”
English: Paul summoned one of the centurions, and said, Bring this young man to the commanding officer, for he has something to tell him.

Limbum: E lor ye a du aègho a fa neè tu yïû goèr, a laa neè ye enáê, “Pol ce e yu ñwáè shañ naè aè ká' máè, a laa neè máè ená m vú neè muu nsuènsuè ca fa neè wáè njobeè' e roèo suñ wáè yuu mo'.”
English: So he took him, and brought him to the commanding officer, and said, Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you, who has something to tell you.

Limbum: Tu yïû goèr yi koo ye aè rkoo, a ye a lá'sïì nyor, e bipshïì neè ye enáê, “Yuu ce wáâ roèo suñ máè yu ká?”
English: The commanding officer took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, What is it that you have to tell me?

Limbum: E laa enáê, “Jus a cu a fa ntañ ená a be laèa neè wáè ená aè vú neè Pol mbe kansuèr aèyaèñseè aèmboè woweèe a ce lá koèñ aè rniñ njep múè mnsa' ca boèñboñ wa'a.
English: He said, The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.

Limbum: Fa byemi ka' njobeè' beèe ce a caèa beèe mkyeèe a be tá' ye aè nduunjïì. Woweèe a ye leè' ená a ka' tá yú Pol ka', a ye yuu ka', ker no yuu ka'. Woweèe a tami nyor seè'ni a ce keè' ená aè byemi gee yuu ce woweèe a be laèa.”
English: Therefore don't yield to them, for more than forty men lie in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they have killed him. Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.

Limbum: Tu yïû goèr yi laa neè ye ená e duê. E duè e fa suñ ñwáè moè' yuu ce e suñ ye naè ka'.
English: So the commanding officer let the young man go, charging him, Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.

Limbum: E m ká' btu mo' a baa ce a m ce faè' njep yeâ tïìi, a laa neè woweèe enáê, “Loèr neè bsoogáè mjeâe mmbaa, ba ñgaâa mnyaèabaèraè' msaèambaê, ba ñgaâa mkoèñ mjeâe mmbaa tá weèe woweèe lo neètú' na aè nyúè búè'úê, duè aè rla' Sisaèriyaè.
English: He called to himself two of the centurions, and said, Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen, and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.

Limbum: Fyá' neè mnyaèabaèraè' mo' tá Pol cu mbo tá weèe lor ye duè aègho boèñboñ duè fa neè Fálïìs ce e yu govanoè.”
English: He asked them to provide animals, that they might set Paul on one, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.

Limbum: Tu yïû goèr yi sañ ñwaè' foñ enáê,
English: He wrote a letter like this:

Limbum: “Ñwaè' ca aè sañ máâ Klaâdïìyoès Lesaè neè wáâ maèsaè Fálïìs ce aè yu govanoè. Máè caè'ni wáè.
English: Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.

Limbum: Máè koñ aè rrïìñ yuu ce a m laèa ená e geèe, a lor ye a du aègho mbe yaèp kansuèr.
English: Desiring to know the cause why they accused him, I brought him down to their council.

Limbum: Máè ka' duè neè ye mbo, a yá máná e m geèe yuu mo' ce aède' a m ba yú ye káè fa ye mbe shañ ka'. Yuu ce a m ce laèa aèmboè ye aè m ba ba buu ce a m ce bipshi neè ye kuu yap ncir.
English: I found him to be accused about questions of their law, but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.

Limbum: Ñwáè aè suñ máè ená Jus a cu mncúè ená a bo tá' ye, koo yú, máè laa máná a lor ye du aègho cárcár fa neè wáè. Máè ker laa foñ neè beèe ce a m ce koèñ aè rsa' mnsa' a Pol naè ená woweèe a vú njep wáâ tïìi, suñ yuu ce e geèe.”
English: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.

Limbum: Bsoogáè a m ku gee aèmboè a m laèa neè woweèe, a lor Pol neètú', a du aègho a ba' aè rla' AÈntipaètidaè.
English: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.

Limbum: Túè' aè ka' raa, woweèe a kútïì yap mbe barakïì, ñgaâa mnyaèabaèraè' a du a Pol weèe.
English: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.

Limbum: Woweèe a ka' duè baè' aè rla' Sisaèriyaè, fa ñwaè' neè govanoè wáá, a fa Pol neè ye foñ.
English: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.

Limbum: Govanoè aè ka' beè' ñwaè' anaè, a bipshi neè Pol ená a ye ñwáâ aè ñgoèñ efá lá? E ka' yu' ená e yu ñwáâ aè ñgoâñ Sïìlesïìyaè,
English: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,

Limbum: a laa enáê, “M be yu'shi wo mnsa' aè nfeè' ce beèe ce weèe woweèe aè m ce sa' mnsa' mbe kansuèr naè a vúè foñ.” E m laèa ená a lor Pol du aègho mbe nto' Hároèd ce ke'nïî.
English: I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive. He commanded that he be kept in Herod's palace.

Limbum: Mnoèñ vi ka' caèa taê, AÈnaèniyaès ce e m ba tu neè ñgaâa tañshi tañshïì aè lor bleebeèe ba loyaè moè' ce a m ce too ená Táètuloè, woweèe a du a suñ govanoè buu ce Pol aè m geèe.
English: After five days, the high priest, Ananias, came down with certain elders and an orator, one Tertullus. They informed the governor against Paul.

Limbum: A ká' Poêl, e ka' vúè, Táètuloè aè ká' a ce suñ govanoè buu ce Pol aè m geèe, a ce laèa neè ye enáê, “Wáè sa' weèr, weèr aè cu neè cumúnyañ-ñwáè seê. AÈ ka' ba njo' buu ce wáè geèe neè weèr, bdïì' wááwá efa yer ñgoèñ vi ba yáánïì.
English: When he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by you we enjoy much peace, and that excellent measures are coming to this nation,

Limbum: Weèr aè byemi yuu ce wáè geèe na aè bdïì' wááwá ba aè nfeè' wááwá, a ce yoèñshi wáè magoèr seê.
English: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.

Limbum: M ce koèñ máná m caasi yoè nfeè' ka', a ce bu' mmbo neè wáè ená aè fa mú nfeè' moè', yu' yuu ce weèr be suñ wáè.
English: But, that I don't delay you, I entreat you to bear with us and hear a few words.

Limbum: Weèr aè yá ñwáè ca aè ba ñwáè ñgá' seê. E ce teèesi btu ese Jus aè ñgoèñ wááwá, a ba tu mo' neè beèe ce a daè' enjep nduunjïì Nyúè ce a too ená Nasaráên.
English: For we have found this man to be a plague, an instigator of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.

Limbum: E m gheèter foñ ená e gee tá Ndap Nyúè ba jaèpri, weèr aè koo ye.
English: He even tried to profane the temple, and we arrested him.

Limbum: Wáè ka' bipshi buu neè ye, wá wáè foñ ku riñ yuu ce yi yu mini kuu buu ce weèr aè suñ wáè ená e geèe na.”
English: By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him.

Limbum: Jus a m beèe njïì Táètuloè, a laa ená buu ce e laèa vi yu mini.
English: The Jews also joined in the attack, affirming that these things were so.

Limbum: Govanoè aè naa bo ená Pol laêa, Pol aè laa enáê, “Máè rïìñ máná wáè sa' to' ca aè bfeè' aèñgoo, máè ce lu'shi aè rsuñ yuu ce yi yu.
English: When the governor had beckoned to him to speak, Paul answered, Because I know that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense,

Limbum: AÈde' wá wáè foñ ku fyá' yá ená káâ' nyúè ce máè m duè aè rla' Jáèrusaláèm aè rloo neè Nyúè vú ba' ntïìni na, ku ba ba mnoèñ ncoèp baa-aè-rrúèú.
English: seeing that you can recognize that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem.

Limbum: Jus a m yá máè ce sár mnsár weèr ñwáè moè' embe Ndaèp Nyúè ka', a ker yá ená máè ce káè' ñgá' aè mndaèp mloo káè aè dïì' mo' aè rla' na ka'.
English: In the temple they didn't find me disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd, either in the synagogues, or in the city.

Limbum: AÈde' woweèe a duñshïì neè wáè ená buu ce a ce suñ ená máè geèe na vi yu mini ka'.
English: Nor can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.

Limbum: Yuu ce m ce byemi a wáâ bsii yi yu ená, m ce loo Nyúè weêr bta aè nduunjïì mo' ce Jus a laèa yap ená a nduunjïû yáánïì ka'. Máè byemi buu wááwá ce a sañ mbe ñwaâ' mncir ba mñwaâ' ñgaâa ncep ntuu Nyúè.
English: But this I confess to you, that after the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets;

Limbum: Máè byemi neè Nyúè, a ce keè' aèmboè woweèe foñ a byemi a ce keè' ená beâe bboèñboñ ba beâe bbebep a be keè fúú efa rkwe naè.
English: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

Limbum: Yi ka' ba wa'a, máè ce gheèter seê, aè rláè ya ntee rara aè nfeè' wááwá aè bsii Nyúè ba ñwáè.
English: Herein I also practice always having a conscience void of offense toward God and men.

Limbum: “Bfeè' mo' vi ka' caèa, máè lo a vúâ a máâ to' tá m bo jaè' ñgaâa ñgá' neè mbaèa, keèr fa rfa neè Nyúè.
English: Now after some years, I came to bring gifts for the needy to my nation, and offerings;

Limbum: Máè ka' ce geèe buu ca, woweèe a vú a yá máè mbe Ndaèp Nyúè. Woweèe a m ce yá máè wa'a, máè geèe neè yuu ce ncir yi laèa ená ñwáè gee tá e bo ba rara aè bsii Nyúè naè wáá, a ba weèr kúr beèe ka', ñgá' moè' aè ba ka'.
English: amid which certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, not with a mob, nor with turmoil.

Limbum: Ka' yi yu wa'a, Jus moâ' aè ñgoâñ Áshaè a m ba aèfo. Woweèe a ba vúè táá a wáâ bsii, laèa yuu, ce yi ka' ba ená woweèe a túr yuu kuu máè.
English: They ought to have been here before you, and to make accusation, if they had anything against me.

Limbum: Ka' beèe ce a vúè na, a ba suñ faèa ce máè m geèe ka' keè táá mbe kansuèr.
English: Or else let these men themselves say what injustice they found in me when I stood before the council,

Limbum: Ku ba yuu yi mo'sir ca ce máè rïìñ máná máè m laèa mbe kansuèr: Máè m laèa mánáê, “Máè táá mbe kansuèr ntïìni na njobeè' máè byemi máná beèe ce a kweñger a be keè fúú efa rkwe.”
English: unless it is for this one thing that I cried standing among them, 'Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged before you today!'

Limbum: Fálïìs ce e m rïìñ nduunjïì anaè boèñboñ seê, aè ku' mnsa', a laa neè woweèe enáê, “Lesaè ce e yu tu yïû goèr neè bsoogáè naè aè ka' vúê, m ka' teni wee mnsa' ca.”
English: But Felix, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way, deferred them, saying, When Lysias, the commanding officer, comes down, I will decide your case.

Limbum: E m laèa neè tu neè bsoogáè rjeèe ená a ke'ni Poêl, a ker laa ená a keè'ni wa'a, a gee tá e ce koo mbáp, ma'shi tá bkar vi a ce vúè ce jaè' ye neè buu.
English: He ordered the centurion that Paul should be kept in custody, and should have some privileges, and not to forbid any of his friends to serve him or to visit him.

Limbum: Mnoèñ mo' vi ka' caèa, Fálïìs aè vú a ñgwa yïì ce a m ce too ená Dusiláè ce aè m ba muu Juês. E tuu beèe, a vú neè Poêl, Pol aè ka' vúè a suñ aèmboè rbyemïû neè Jisos Kraêis, e ce yu'shi.
English: But after some days, Felix came with Drusilla, his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.

Limbum: Pol aè ka' káè' ce suñ aèmboè ñgeâe yáánïì ba aèmboè aède' ñwáè kur ntee ker ba aèmboè noèñ mnsa' Nyúè, Fálïìs aè wáêp, a laa enáê, “Wáè laèa yi gháá seè'ni. Duè yo yu. M be koni fáñ tá m ka' keèr tuu beèe tá a vú neè wáè.”
English: As he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, and answered, Go your way for this time, and when it is convenient for me, I will summon you.

Limbum: E m ce kwaè'shi foñ ená Pol be yuni ye. E ka' ce kwaè'shi wa'a, a ce ká' Pol aèfo aèfo a ce de' a ye.
English: Meanwhile, he also hoped that money would be given to him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore also he sent for him more often, and talked with him.

Limbum: Bfeè' vi ka' caâa bbaa, Poshoè Fástoès aè lor dïû' Fálïìs, a ba aè govanoè. Fálïìs aè m ce koèñ ená e gee tá nyor boñ Juês. E ka' koèñ wa'a, a ku lá Pol mbe shañ.
English: But when two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and desiring to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in bonds.

Limbum: Mnoèñ vi ka' caâa btaar, ká' embe nfeè' ce Fástoès aè m koo nta', Fástoès aè natïû aè rla' Sisaèriyaè a du aè rla' Jáèrusaláèm.
English: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

Limbum: E ka' baè', beâe bgoèrgoèr efa múè ñgaâa tañshi tañshïì ba btu efa múè Jus a vúê, a yá ye a suñ ye buu ce Pol aè m geèe. Woweèe a m laèa neè ye tatap
English: Then the high priest and the principal men of the Jews informed him against Paul, and they begged him,

Limbum: ená e gee yuu ce nyor boñ woweèe, laa tá Pol vú aè rla' Jáèrusaláèm. Woweèe a m laèa wa'a njobeè' woweèe a m cu mncúè ená Pol aè ka' ce vúè, baná woweèe a be tá' aè nduunjïì, koo yú.
English: asking a favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem; plotting to kill him on the way.

Limbum: Fástoès aè beesïì neè woweèe ená Pol yu aè rla' Sisaèriyaè, beèe a ce keè'ni ye aèfo, baná e be cu ba mnoèñ múcaèr, kúti aè rla' anaè.
English: However Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.

Limbum: E m laèa neè woweèe ená a ma'shi tá a btu efa waâp mú a du aè rla' Sisaèriyaè, ka' ba ená e geèe yuu mo' bebep, tá woweèe a bo laèa yuu ce a túr aè rlaèa kuu ye.
English: Let them therefore, said he, that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.

Limbum: E ka' cu a woweèe aèmboè mnoèñ waami káè mnoèñ rúú wa'a, a nati a du aè rla' Sisaèriyaè. Túè' aè ka' raa, e niñ mbe kor aè rsa' mnsa', a laa ená a vú neè Poêl.
English: When he had stayed among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.

Limbum: Pol aè ka' vúè, Jus ce a m vúâ aè rla' Jáèrusaláèm naè a vú a tááte, a sir ye a fa mbetar, a suñ ku' buu ce e m geèe. Geewa'a yuu mo' yi m ba ce yi m ce duèñshi ená buu anaè aè m ba mini ka'.
English: When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing against him many and grievous charges which they could not prove,

Limbum: Pol aè kanïì, a laa enáê, “Máè geèe faèa moè' kuu mncir Juês, ba Ndap Nyúè ka', a gee faèa moè' neè ñkúú aè to' Rum ka'.”
English: while he said in his defense, Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.

Limbum: Fástoès aè ka' ce koèñ aè rgeèe tá nyor boñ Juês, e laa neè Pol enáê, “Wáè koèñ aè rduè aè rla' Jáèrusaláèm tá m sa' wo mnsa' ca ba aèfo a?”
English: But Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem, and be judged by me there concerning these things?

Limbum: Pol aè beesïì enáê, “M táá seè'ni ba mbe kor ñkwe Ruêm, aè ba mbe dïì' ce a be sa' wa mnsa'. Máè geèe faèa moè' neè Jus ka', wá wáè foñ rïìñ wa'a.
English: But Paul said, I am standing before Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.

Limbum: Ka' ba ená máè bú' ncir a gee yuu mo' ce a ba yú máè, m kanïì efa rkwe ka'. Ka' ba ená buu ce Jus a laèa aèmboè máè na vi yu mini ka', ñwáè moè' túr ñger aè rkoo máè fa neè woweèe ka'. M ce koèñ máná a sa' wa mnsa' ba njeptii ñkwe Ruêm.”
English: For if I have done wrong, and have committed anything worthy of death, I don't refuse to die; but if none of those things is true that they accuse me of, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!

Limbum: Fástoès aè du a de' a yïì beèe ce a m ce cep ye, a laa enáê, “Wáè laèa wáná ñkwe Rum be sa' wo mnsa', baná a be duè yá ba ye.”
English: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.

Limbum: Mnoèñ mo' vi ka' caèa, ñkúú Agripaè ba Báènis a du aè rla' Sisaèriyaè aè rcaè'ni Fástoès.
English: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea, and greeted Festus.

Limbum: Woweèe a ka' cu aèfo aè mú mnoèñ mo', Fástoès aè suñ mnsa' Pol neè ñkúú. E m suñ ye enáê, “Ñwáè moè' yu aèfa ce Fálïìs aè m ce duè, a lá aèfa aè ñwáè shañ.
English: As he stayed there many days, Festus laid Paul's case before the king, saying, There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;

Limbum: Máè ka' duè aè rla' Jáèrusaláèm, beâe bgoèrgoèr efa múè ñgaâa tañshi tañshïì ba bleebeèe efa múè Jus a suñ buu ce e geèe, a laa ená m laa máná e gweè mnsa'.
English: about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, asking for a sentence against him.

Limbum: Máè suñ woweèe ená ndeèe Rum yu ená a ka' vú neè ñwáè ce e geèe faèa, baná beèe ce a laèa ená e geèe faèa naè, a be vúè, tá ye ye laa yuu kuu faèa ce a laèa ená e geèe, tá a ka' teni mnsa'.
English: To whom I answered that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction, before the accused has met the accusers face to face, and has had opportunity to make his defense concerning the matter laid against him.

Limbum: Weèr woweèe aè ka' vúè aèfa, máè caasïì nfeè' ka'. Túè' aè ka' raa, máè niñ mbe kor aè rsa' mnsa', a laa máná a vú neè ñwáè anaè.
English: When therefore they had come together here, I didn't delay, but on the next day sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought.

Limbum: Beèe ce a m laèa ená e geèe faèa naè a táá mbe koêr, a laa yuu mo' efa buu bbebep ce máè m ce kwaè'shi ená woweèe a be laèa aèmboè ye ka'.
English: Concerning whom, when the accusers stood up, they brought no charge of such things as I supposed;

Limbum: Yuu ce woweèe a m laèa yi m ku ba ba aèmboè mnsár ce a woweèe a m ce sár aèmboè njáèá njïì ce a woweèe a ke loo neè Nyúè, ker ba foñ aèmboè ñwáè moè' ce e m kwe, ce a m ce too ená Jisoès ce Pol aè m ce laèa ená e cu nteèe naè.
English: but had certain questions against him about their own religion, and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

Limbum: Máè riñ yuu ce aède' máè m ba gee kuu yuu ce a m ce sár mnsár aètu mo naè ka'. Yi ka' ba wa'a, máè laa neè ye máná e be koèñ aè rduè aè rla' Jáèrusaláèm duè sa' vi mnsa' aèfo lá?
English: Being perplexed how to inquire concerning these things, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.

Limbum: Pol aè laa ená a caasi vi mnsa' tá du teni ba Taèr Mañgoèñ, máè laa máná a ku ce ke'ni ye caar tá nfeè' ce m be tuusi ye neè ñkwe Rum ka' gháá.”
English: But when Paul had appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor, I commanded him to be kept until I could send him to Caesar.

Limbum: Agripaè aè laa neè Fástoès enáê, “M be koèñ foñ aè ryu' yuu ce ñwáè anaè be laèa.” Fástoès aè beesïì enáê, “AÈ be yu' yuu ce e be laèa ba aèyaèñseè.”
English: Agrippa said to Festus, I also would like to hear the man myself. Tomorrow, he said, you shall hear him.

Limbum: Túè' aè ka' raa, Agripaè ba Báènis a vú neè foèo-ñwáè, a niñ mbe ndaèp rcuteè. A m niñ mbo a beèe ce a m ba btu neè bsoogáè, ba beâe bgoèrgoâr aè rla' ca. Fástoès aè laêa, a vú neè Poêl.
English: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and they had entered into the place of hearing with the commanding officers and principal men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.

Limbum: A ka' vúè neè ye, e laa enáê, “Ñkúú Agripaè ker ba beèe wááwá ce weèr woweèe yu taâa, yá neè ñwáè ce Jus wááwá a m tuu beèe ená a vú yá máè, suñ buu ce e geèe. Woweèe a vú a yá máè aè rla' Jáèrusaláèm, ker ba aèfa, a ce waani, a ce laèa ená e yu ñwáè ce e ba keèr cu nteèe ka'.
English: Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

Limbum: Máè m fyá' a yá máná e bú' ncir ka', a gee yuu mo' bebep ce aède' a m ba yú ye yú ka', aè ka' ba njobeè' e m koèñ ená Taèr Mañgoèñ sa' vi mnsa', máè laa máná m be tuusi ye neè ye.
English: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor I determined to send him.

Limbum: Ka' yi yu wa'a, máè yá yuu mo' ce e geèe ce máè ba sañ suñ Tata ka'. A mbuèu ce máè vúè neè ye njep weâe tïìi, lañlañ njeptii wáè ce ñkúú Agripaè, tá seâe ce fyá' nje múè mnsa' ca tá m bo túr yuu ce m sañ.
English: Of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him forth before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, that, after examination, I may have something to write.

Limbum: Yi yu yáánïì ená m tuusi ñwáè shañ ce máè buu efa rsañ, suñ yuu ce e geèe ka'.”
English: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to also specify the charges against him.

Limbum: Agripaè aè laa neè Pol enáê, “Máè fa wáè njïì ená aè laa eku wáâ cuèu.” Pol aè naa bo mbekïì a laa yuu. E m laèa enáê,
English: Agrippa said to Paul, You may speak for yourself. Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.

Limbum: “Ñkúú Agripaè, máè yá máná máè koni rboâñtu ntïìni na aè rtáá a wáâ bsii laèa yuu kuu buu wááwá ce Jus a laèa kuu máè.
English: I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you this day concerning all the things that I am accused by the Jews,

Limbum: Woweèe a rïìñ máè ká' ese aè nfeè' njïìsaèp seê. Woweèe a ka' koñ aè rlaèa, aède' a ku laa ená máè m ba moè' efa múè beèe ce a ke geèe mcáâr aè njáèá njïì ce a ke loo neè yaèp Nyúè ka', a cu aèmboè ñwáè Farïìsïî.
English: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

Limbum: Máè táá mbena seè'ni aè mnsa' njobeè' máè byemi, a ce keè' buu ce Nyúè aè m kaè' neè viseèe btaê,
English: Now I stand here to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,

Limbum: aè ba buu ce viseèe mntáâ' ncoèp baa-aè-rrúèú a ce loo neè Nyúè neètú' ba neèmootïì, a ce keè' foñ ená a be koni vi. Taèr Mañgoèñ, yu njobeè' rbyemïì ca ce ená Jus a loèr máè aè mnsa'.
English: which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa!

Limbum: Yi yu tatap neè weèe aè rbyemi ená Nyúè e ke fúr beèe ce a kweñger efa rkwe njoká?
English: Why is it judged incredible with you, if God does raise the dead?

Limbum: “Má máè foñ aè m kwaè'shi máná máè ba geèe yuu wááwá ce aède' m geêe, aè rkani buu ce vi m ba kuu Jisoès aè rla' Nasaráèt.
English: I myself most certainly thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

Limbum: Taèr Mañgoèñ, nyúè aè ka' kuèu ñgoèñ, máè yá aèmboè rraa li raa embe buèu, mbe máâ nduè, ker ba aè nduè beèe ce weèr woweèe aè m ce duè. Rraa anaè li m raa a caa nyúè.
English: at noon, O king, I saw on the way a light from the sky, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who traveled with me.

Limbum: Weèr wááwá aè gweñgeèr aè nsheè, máè yu' aèmboè njeèndoñ ce laèa neè máè aè li Hibruè enáê, ‘Soêl, Soêl, AÈ ce fa máè ñgá' njoká? Wáè ka' yá luèr ku túú kuèu njo, baná yi be yañ ba wáè.’
English: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.'

Limbum: Máè beesïì mánáê, ‘Tataê, a wáè nda?’ Tata aè laa enáê, ‘A máè Jisoès ce aè ce jar neè ye naè.
English: I said, 'Who are you, Lord?' He said, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

Limbum: Naèti táá mbekïì, njobeè' máè vúè tá m bo ce wáè aè yaè ñwáè rfaè', ker ba aè ñwáè ce aè be ce suñ beèe buu ce wáè yá ese máè ntïìni na, ker ba vïì ce m be loè duèñshi wáè.
English: But arise, and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things which you have seen, and of the things which I will reveal to you;

Limbum: M be fúr wáè embaè mmbo beèe Isráèl, ba embaè mmbo beèe enje jáá.
English: delivering you from the people, and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,

Limbum: M ce tuu wáè ená aè du mú' map mmir, gee tá woweèe a fúú efa túè'nji du aè rraa, lo enjeptii Sataèn du njeptii Nyúè, tá a bo foèosi woweèe efa yaèp buu bbebep, tá woweèe a koni dïì' aè múè beèe ce Nyúè aè geèe woweèe a ba brara njobeè' woweèe a byemi neè máè naè.’
English: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me.'

Limbum: “Yi ka' ba wa'a, ñkúú Agripaè, máè kani efa rgeèe yuu ce Nyúè aè m suñ máè aè njáèá rlo mo' naè ka'.
English: Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,

Limbum: Pol aè ka' ce laèa buu ca aè njáâá wa'a, Fástoès aè waa, a laa enáê, “Poêl, tu yi ce kar wáè embo! Ku' yo ñwaè' ce wáè yá'ni anaè yi geèe wáè ce baa.”
English: As he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, you are crazy! Your great learning is driving you insane!

Limbum: Pol aè beesïì enáê, “Maèsaè Fástoès, tu yi ce kar máè embo ka', buu ce m ce laèa vi yu mini, a ba neè bfee-ñwáè.
English: But he said, I am not crazy, most excellent Festus, but boldly declare words of truth and reasonableness.

Limbum: Ñkúú rïìñ buu ca. M ka' ce laèa neè ye m ker ce wáp yuu mo' ka'. Máè rïìñ neè mini-ñwáè ená e máñni mo' efa buu ca ka' njobeè' a m geèe vi ba aè bsúèti ka'.
English: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak freely. For I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.

Limbum: Ñkúú Agripaè, wáè byemi yuu ce ñgaâa ncep ntuu Nyúè a m laèa a? Máè rïìñ máná wáè byemi.”
English: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.

Limbum: Agripaè aè laa neè Pol enáê, “AÂ kwaè'shi ená aède' aè ku lor nfeè' múcaècaèr wa'a, gee m ba ñwáè rbyemïì a?”
English: Agrippa said to Paul, With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?

Limbum: Pol aè laa enáê, “Káè yu nfeè' yïû múcaèr áè, káè yu yïû njïìsaèp áè, m ce loo neè Nyúè máná wáè ker ba beèe wááwá ce a ce yu' yuu ce m ce laèa ntïìni na, a ba ba aèmboè má máè yu na, ke' ba ñgaâa shañ foñ aèmboè máè ka'.”
English: Paul said, I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me this day, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.

Limbum: Ñkúú ba govanoè ba Báènïîs, ker ba bár beèe wááwá a natïì mbekïì.
English: The king rose up with the governor, and Bernice, and those who sat with them.

Limbum: A ka' naèti duè, a seèesïî, a laa enáê, “Ñwáè ca ce geèe yuu mo' ce aède' a ba yú ye káè fa ye aè shañ ka'.”
English: When they had withdrawn, they spoke one to another, saying, This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

Limbum: Agripaè aè laa neè Fástoès enáê, “Ñwáè ca aè ka' tá baè laèa ená ñkwe Rum a ñwáè ce e be sa' vi mnsa' ka', seèe aè ba maè'shi ye tá e duê.”
English: Agrippa said to Festus, This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.

Limbum: A ka' seèesi ená weèr Pol weèe be niñ mbe keñ ñgoèr duè aè to' Italeè, a lor Pol ba ñgaâa shañ mo' a fa neè tu neè bsoogáè rjeèe efa bkúr bsoogáè ñkwe Ruêm. A m ce too ñwáè ca ená Julïìyoès.
English: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.

Limbum: Weèr aè m niñ mbe keñ ñgoèr ce aè m ba yïû aè dïì' ce a m ce too ená AÈdamituèm. Keñ anaè aè m táá aè rco'ti duè, ce táátá aè mla' moâ' aèwaâa roè aè ñgoâñ Áshaè. Weèr aè niñ mbo a ce duè. AÈristakoès ce aè m ba ñwáâ aè rla' Táèsaèlonikaâ aè ñgoâñ Máèsáèdonïìyaè aè m ba weèr woweèe.
English: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea; Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

Limbum: Túè' aè ka' raa, weèr aè ba' aè rla' Sidoèn. Julïìyoès aè gee ñgeâe boèñboñ neè Poêl. E m maè'shi ye e du a yá bkar vi tá woweèe a bo keè' aè ye.
English: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.

Limbum: Weèr aè loâ aèfo a niñ mbe keñ a ce duè, fu' yi ka' ce vúâ aè mbeèp ce keñ aè m ce duè, weèr aè lá' aè mbeèp moâ' aè ñgoâñ Saiproès ce fu' yi m ce caèa ka'.
English: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

Limbum: Weèr aè ka' tuu roâ aè ñgoâñ Sïìlesïìyaè ba aè ñgoâñ Paèmfilïìyaè a du a ba' aè rla' Miraè aè ñgoâñ Lishaè.
English: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

Limbum: Weèr aè ka' baè' aèfo, tu neè bsoogáè rjeèe yi yá keñ yïû aè rla' AÈláèksandaè ce e m ce duè aè to' Italeè, a fa weèr mbo.
English: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.

Limbum: Weèr aè m ce duè múwáèá-múwáèá, a lor mnoèñ aèñgoo, a yá ñgá' seê, a ka' ba' aètútú rla' Kidoèm. Fu' yi m maè'shi ená weèr ba' aè rla' anaè ka', weèr aè lá' a du aè mbeèp moâ' aègee to' Kreât ce fu' yi m ce caèa ka'. Rla' Saèlmoneè li ba yi nje yáá.
English: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

Limbum: Keñ aè ce dii aèwaâa roè, weèr aè yá ñgá' seê, a ka' ba' aè dïì' ce a m ce too ená Fáá Háváèn aègee rla' Lisïìyaè.
English: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.

Limbum: Weèr aè m caèasi nfeè' aè nduunjïì goèr seê. Rjáèr li m ba neè mluè-ñwáè seê, njobeè' noèñ ce a ke tañshi tañshïû goèr yi m caèa, aè m ba aè cuèu saa.
English: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous, because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them,

Limbum: Yi ka' ba wa'a, Pol aè báá woweèe a laa enáê, “Beèe caê, máè yá máná liseèe rjáèr ca li be ba yáánïì ka'. Seèe ka' loâ aèfa baná yïìseèe buu be bep, tá keñ bep, tá beèe a kweñger foñ.”
English: and said to them, Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.

Limbum: Geewa'a, tu neè bsoogáè rjeèe yi m byemi ba yuu ce ñwáè ce e m ce doèo keñ ker ba ñwáè ce e m túr keñ anaè a m laèa.
English: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.

Limbum: Dïì' ce woweèe a m vúè táá aèfo anaè aè m ba dïû' boèñboñ aè rcu aè saa ka'. Beèe magoèr a fa ntañ ená a gheter yá ená a be baè' aè rla' Fenïìs cu ba aèfo lá. Fenïìs aè m ba dïì' moâ' aè to' Kreât ce bkeñ vi m ce vúè ce táá, ka' ker ce co'ti ce duè. AÈ m ba dïì' ce wáè m ka' ba táá ce keè' mbaè mbuèuntii, aè ku yá rdip aè yo bo ñkoèp ba yo bo maè'.
English: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking northeast and southeast.

Limbum: Mú fu' mo' yi ce vúè embaè mbuèuñgoèñ, woweèe a kwa'shïì ená a koni yuu ce a ce roèo. Woweèe a súñ ma co' ce keñ aè m táá aègho a lá mbe keñ a co'ti a ce duè aèwaâa roâ aè to' Kreêt.
English: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.

Limbum: Woweèe a m duè njïìsaèp ka', ma nteèendúñ moè' aè suâu aè to' Kreêt, aè ba yïì ce a too enáê, Yïû aè bke'.
English: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.

Limbum: Nteèendúñ anaè aè koo aè keñ, keñ aè moo aè rduè laèr, weèr aè boñlaèr a ma'shïî, e lor keñ a ce duè aègho.
English: When the ship was caught, and couldn't face the wind, we gave way to it, and were driven along.

Limbum: Weèr aè caa a du aè ñgúè' moâ' aè rla' Kaèwudaè ce fu' yi m ce caèa ka', a gheter seê, tá keñ ñká' ce a m cúú mbaè mbuèu yïû ñgoèr anaè ka' bep ka'.
English: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.

Limbum: A m súèñ a niñ aègho mbe múè yïû ñgoèr, a fyáá bkúè a kur keñ ñgoèr aègho faè dïì' e sa'ñger ka'. Woweèe a ka' ce wáp ená keñ be baè' Sitïì, niñ njep múè nsaruñ táá, woweèe a suusïì ma co' ce keñ aè m ce táá aègho naè njep múè roè tá keñ bo táá, keñ aè ku ce duè neè yi bo.
English: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.

Limbum: Nteèendúñ ca aè ku ce caèa, a ce fa weèr ñgá' seê. Túè' aè ka' raa, woweèe a ká' a ce fúshi buu embe keñ a ce maè'ri njep roè.
English: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.

Limbum: Mnoèñ vi ka' baâ' btaar, woweèe a lor buu mfaè' embe keñ neè map mmbo, a ma'ri njep roè.
English: On the third day, they threw out the ship's tackle with their own hands.

Limbum: Mnoèñ vi m caèa aèñgoo seê, weèr aè be yá rlir nyúè káè mkaèñsïì ka', nteèendúñ aè ku ce caèa tatap seê. Weèr aè riñ ená aède' weèr luñ efa gho ka'.
English: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.

Limbum: Beèe ca a ka' cu teèteè seê, ye yuu ka', Pol aè natïì a táá a waâp mú a laa enáê, “Beèe caê, weèe aè mú yu' yuu ce máè mú laa neè weèe aè to' Kreât naè, cu aèfo, yïìseèe buu aè ba keèr bep, bú aè cicïì ka'.
English: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them, and said, Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete, and have gotten this injury and loss.

Limbum: M ce laèa neè weèe seè'ni na ená weèe kur ntee. Moè' efa weèe be kwe ka'. Yuu ce yi be bep, saè'ñger, ku ba keñ caè'caè'.
English: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

Limbum: AÈ ba neètú', Nyúè ce e túr máè, ce máâ ke loo neè ye, aè tuusïì yïì ncïìndap, e vú a táá a máâ geñ,
English: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,

Limbum: a laa enáê, ‘Poêl, fa wáp ka'. AÈ be kuè táá aè bsii Sisaè. Nyúè aè túr wáè aè ntee boèñboñ, a ja' myoâñ beèe ce weèe woweèe yu mbe keñ na njo' wáè.’
English: saying, 'Don't be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.'

Limbum: Beèe caê, baná weèe kur ntee njobeè' máè byemi máná yi be kuè ba aèmboè Nyúè aè laèa neè máè.
English: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.

Limbum: Geewa'a, keñ be niñ nje múè nsaruñ, taèñte, táá aèwaâa rla' mo'.”
English: But we must run aground on a certain island.

Limbum: AÈ ka' ba neètú' ce mnoèñ vi baè' war ncoèp-kyeèe-aè-rrúèú, nteèendúñ aè ku ce daè' neè weèr aè rdip ce a m ce too ená AÈnduyaè. AÈ ba aèmboè neè ntee tú' wa'a, beèe ce a m ce doèo keñ a yu' enjep bláá ená woweèe a ce baè' aèwaâa roè.
English: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.

Limbum: Woweèe a lor kúè, a cúú yuu rïìr rir aè cuèu efa gho, a suusi njep roè a yá ená rcoomïì efa rdip anaè li yu aèmboè mkoo mbaa. A ka' keèr duè mú ntaèm moè', a ker suusi kúè anaè njo a yá ená rcoomïì efa gho li yu mkoo ncoèp-ta-aè-rrúèú.
English: They took soundings, and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.

Limbum: Woweèe a wáp ená keñ be kuèu nyor aè bluèr njep múè roè, a lor bco' ce keñ e ke táá aègho njep múè roè naè embaè mbuèu keñ vi kyeèe, a fa njep roè, a loo ená túè' raa cárcár.
English: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.

Limbum: Beèe ce a m ce doèo keñ ca a gheteèr ená a ba cañ fúú embo, a lor keñ ñká' a suusi njep roè, a bo'shi ená woweèe a ce duè kuè cuâu keñ tá a bo keèr fúr bco' mo' ce keñ e ke táá aègho njep roè naè.
English: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship, and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,

Limbum: Pol aè laa neè tu neè bsoogáè rjeèe ba bsoogáè enáê, “Beèe ca a ka' tá kuè cu mbe keñ na ka', weèe luñ ka'.”
English: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Unless these stay in the ship, you can't be saved.

Limbum: Bsoogáè a ceeshïì bkúè efa keñ ñká', e ce duè mbaè roè.
English: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat, and let it fall off.

Limbum: Túè' aè ka' káè' ce raa, Pol aè bu' mmbo neè woweèe wááwá ená woweèe a ye yuu. E m laèa neè woweèe enáê, “Weèe aè yá mluè, a cu neè njeè aè mnoèñ ncoèp-kyeèe-aè-rrúèú, a joo yuu kuè cuèu ka'.
English: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.

Limbum: Baná m ce bu' mmbo neè weèe ená weèe ye yuu. Weèe aè ka' tá ye yuu ka', weèe luñ ka'. Mbúè nyúè'tu embe tu ñwáè moè' efa weâe mú be duè aè yuu ka'.”
English: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.

Limbum: Pol aè ka' laèa buu ca neè woweèe mïìsi, a lor bráêd, a loo a yoñshi Nyúè aè waâp bsii, a bá' a ká' a ce ye.
English: When he had said this, and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all, and he broke it, and began to eat.

Limbum: Ca yi m fa woweèe ñger, woweèe a waseè, a ye yuu.
English: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.

Limbum: Weèr aè m ba mbe keñ anaè wááwá beèe mjeâe mbaa neè ncoèp-ntuunfu-aè- mnsaèambaê.
English: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.

Limbum: Woweèe a ka' ye byee yu' boèñboñ, a fúshi msañ ce mi m ba mbe keñ a ma' njep roè tá keñ bo fáp.
English: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.

Limbum: Túè' aè ka' raa, woweèe a yá nje waa ñkúè, a riñ faèdïì' ce woweèe a m ba anaè ka', a ka' ce fyá', a yá dïì' mo' ce rdip li tuñ a bársïî, nsaruñ aè ba aèwaâa roè anaè seê. Woweèe a kwa'shi ená yi ka' ba aètáèr woweèe a doo keñ anaè du aègho mbe dïì' anaè, tá e bo niñ njep múè nsaruñ táá.
English: When it was day, they didn't recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.

Limbum: Woweèe a ceeshïì bco' ce keñ e ke táá aègho njep múè roè, vi suu njep roè, a ker ba'shi bkúè ce a ke kur yuu ce a ke doèo keñ aègho. Woweèe a ka' geèe wa' mïìsi, a naa ma cáâ' báèbár ce yi m ba kuè cuâu keñ tá fu' yi bo koo njo, doèo keñ duè aègho.
English: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.

Limbum: Geewa'a, keñ aè niñ njep múè nsaruñ yïì embe dïì' ce mdip mi m ce tarte a mmo', a táá. Cuâu keñ yi niñ njep múè nsaruñ anaè boèñboñ seê, a tañte njo. Mdip ce mi m ce bañti ce vúè neè ñger-ñwáè se naè, mi sa'sïì mbuèu keñ.
English: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.

Limbum: Bsoogáè a fa ntañ ená a be yúshi ñgaâa shañ ce a m ba mbe keñ anaè wááwá faè dïì' moè' efa woweèe bo coo njep roè bu' rdip, fúú nje waa ñkúè cañ ka'.
English: The soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.

Limbum: Tu neè bsoogáè rjeèe yi m ce koèñ aè rjaè' Pol efa rkwe, a kani woweèe efa ryúshi ñgaâa shañ. E m laèa ená beèe ce a rïìñ aè rbu' rdip a nyáá coo njep roè entombïì bu' rdip, du nje waa ñkúè.
English: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;

Limbum: Yi m ba ená bár beèe mo' a ba'ni plaêñ, tá bár mo' a ba'ni bbaèbaèr keñ ce e m saè'ñger naè. A m geèe wa'a, weèr woweèe wááwá aè du a ba' nje waa ñkúè, yuu mo' yi joo ñwáè moè' ka'.
English: and the rest should follow, some on planks, and some on other things from the ship. So it happened that they all escaped safely to the land.

Limbum: Weèr aè ka' baè' nje waa ñkúè, luèñ efa ñgá', a yu' ená rlii rla' ce rdip li m sïìr a tarte anaè li yu ená Málitaè.
English: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.

Limbum: Beâe aè rla' anaè a m geèe ñgeâe boèñboñ neè weèr, a caa embe dïì' ce weèr aè m ce kwaè'shi. Woweèe a m koni weèr, a too mor njobeè' mbeèñ aè m ce gweè, mbáp aè ce fúte.
English: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire, and received us all, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

Limbum: Pol aè baashïì ñguu a byá' mbe rkoo, a ka' ce toèo, nyo aè fúú enjo njobeè' mor yi m luèu goèr, a luu ye aè boè, a barni aègho.
English: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

Limbum: Beâe aè rla' anaè a ka' yá aèmboè nyo ce láñláñ ye aè boè, woweèe a laa fa waâp mú enáê, “Ñwáè anaè ku ba ñwáè ce e yú ñwáè. Ka' e luèñ efa rkwe enjep roè wa'a, e ku bii nyaèa rkwe.”
English: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said one to another, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.

Limbum: Pol aè kar nyo ca efa boè, e gwe njep mor, yuu mo' yi gee ye ka'.
English: However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn't harmed.

Limbum: Woweèe a m ce keè' ená bo yi ka' tá kuè ko' ye mbe dïì' ka', baná e be kuè loè co'ti gweè aè nsheè, kwe. Woweèe a cu nfeè' njïìsaèp seê, a yá yuu mo' yi gee ye ka', woweèe a kupseè map mkwaè'shïì a laa enáê, “E yu nyúè moè'.”
English: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

Limbum: Ñwáâ ñgoâr aè rla' anaè aè m túr ñkúè aètútú. A m ce too ye ená Puèbilïìyoès. E m koni weèr, a nyañ weèr boèñboñ se aè mnoâñ btaar.
English: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us, and courteously entertained us for three days.

Limbum: Yïì ta aè m noèñ a ce yañ. Mbáp aè m ce fúte ye, e ker ce to' a ce fïìñshi. Pol aè niñ mbe dïì' e m noèñ, a gee rloo, a lá mmbo mbe yeâ nduè, e ke'seè.
English: It happened that the father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him.

Limbum: Ca yi ka' koni wa'a, bár ñgaâa byañ ce a m ba aè rla' anaè a vúseè, Pol aè gee woweèe a ke'seè.
English: Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came, and were cured.

Limbum: Woweèe a m naèa weèr aè mnduunjïû jáá jáèá jáá. Weèr aè ka' niñ mbe keñ tá weèr bo ce duè, woweèe a fa weèr buu ce vi bo jaè' weèr.
English: They also honored us with many honors, and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.

Limbum: Weèr aè m cu aè rla' ca aè mñwáá btaar a ka' co'ti a ce duè mbe keñ yïû aè rla' AÈláèksandaè ce a m ce too ená Mfar Mnyúè. E m táá aè rla' ca njep múè roè káâ' aè cuèu saa caar saa aè mïî.
English: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose sign was The Twin Brothers.

Limbum: Weèr aè du a ba' aè rla' Sïìrakusaè a cu aèfo mnoâñ btaar.
English: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

Limbum: Weèr aè ka' loâ aèfo a kaari a ba' aè rla' Rágïìyoèm. Túè' aè ka' raa, fu' yi ká' a ce vúè embaè mbuèuñgoèñ. Túè' moè' aè ka' raa, weèr aè ba' aè rla' Puètolïì.
English: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,

Limbum: Weèr aè m yá bfúr mo' aèfo, woweèe a laa ená weèr woweèe cu aèfo aè mnoèñ saèambaê. Awá weèr aè du a ba' aè rla' Ruêm.
English: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.

Limbum: Tá weèr ka' baè' aè rla' Ruêm, bfúr ce aè rla' anaè a m banïì yu' ená weèr yu aè nduunjïì. Woweèe a vú caar a ba' aè ntaa yïû aè rla' AÈpiyoè, beèe mo' a ba' faèdïì' bhoètál vi m ba vi btaar, tá a bo koni weèr. Pol aè ka' yá woweèe, a yoñshi Nyúè, ñger yi vú ye nje nyoèr.
English: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God, and took courage.

Limbum: Weèr aè ka' baè' aè rla' Ruêm, a ma'shi Poêl, e ce cu neè yi tu, ñwáè soogáè moè' aè ce keè'ni ye.
English: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.

Limbum: Mnoèñ vi ka' caâa btaar, e ká' beâe bgoèrgoèr efa múè Jus ce aè rla' Ruêm. Woweèe a ka' vúè, e laa neè woweèe enáê, “Yaè beèe, ka' máè m geèe faèa moè' neè yïìseèe beèe káè ma' ndeèe to' ce viseèe btarkú a m láè neè seèe naè ka' wa'a, a ku koo máè aè rla' Jáèrusaláèm, a fa mbe mmbo beèe ñkwe Ruêm.
English: It happened that after three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,

Limbum: Beèe ñkwe Rum ca a m bipshi buu neè máè, a koñ aè rmaè'shi máè njobeè' máè m geèe yuu mo' ce a m ba yú máè aètu mo ka'.
English: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.

Limbum: Geewa'a, Jus a ka' kani ená a fa maè'shi máè ka', máè boñlaèr a laa máná wa mnsa' be sa' ñkwe Ruêm. Máè m laèa wa'a, a ke' túr yuu bebep mo' aè rlaèa kuu yaè beèe ka'.
English: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation.

Limbum: A mbuèu ce máè laèa máná weèe vúê, tá m yá weèe, tá seèe de'. Kwaèñ yu máè kuè rkoo seè'ni na ba aètu ñwáè ce beèe Isráèl a m cu a ce keè'.”
English: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

Limbum: Woweèe a beesïì enáê, “Weèr aè be koo mñwaè' moâ' aè ñgoâñ Juèdiyaè ce a sañ a kuu wáè ka'. Nfúr yïìseèe moè' aè be vúâ aèfo neè nsuñ moâ' mbembep káè a laa yuu bebep mo' kuu wáè ka'.
English: They said to him, We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.

Limbum: Ka' yi yu wa'a, weèr ce koèñ aè rrïìñ yuu ce aè ce kwaè'shi njobeè' weèr rïìñ werná beèe wááwá a ce laèa bebep kuu njáèá nduunjïì ce aè yu njo na.”
English: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.

Limbum: A Pol weèe a seesïì a lá noèñ ce woweèe a be vúè yá ye. Noèñ anaè yi ka' gháá, woweèe a vú seê, a caa aèmboè woweèe a m ba naè, a yá Pol mbe dïì' ce e m ce cu. E m suñ woweèe aèmboè kúú Nyúè, a nashi buu ca neè woweèe káâ' aè ñgaèptú' du ba' aè mbuèuñkuèr. E m gheèter aè rgeèe tá woweèe a byemi neè Jisoès, a ce fyá' mbe mñwaâ' mncir Musïìs, ba mñwaâ' ñgaâa ncep ntuu Nyúè aè rduèñshi ená Jisoès yu Kraâis anaè.
English: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about the Kingdom of God, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening.

Limbum: Beèe mo' a m byemi yuu ce e m laèa, beèe mo' a byemi yap yu ka'.
English: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.

Limbum: Woweèe a m túr mñgaèpni fa waâp mú kuu yuu ce Pol aè m laèa, a ka' naèti ce duè, Pol aè laa mbúè laèa neè woweèe. E m laèa enáê, “Yú' Rara yi m laèa yuu yáánïì neè weêe btarkú mbe nfeè' ce e m tuu AÈsayaè ce e m ba ñwáè ncep ntuu Nyúè, e vú a laa enáê,
English: When they didn't agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one word, The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah, the prophet, to our fathers,

Limbum: ‘Duè yá beèe ca laa neè woweèe enáê, “Weèe be yu' keèr yu', yu' ka'. Weèe be keè' keèr keè', yá ka'.
English: saying, 'Go to this people, and say, in hearing, you will hear, but will in no way understand. In seeing, you will see, but will in no way perceive.

Limbum: Yi yu wa'a njobeè' mntee beèe ca vi tap seê. Btuè' vi lo' woweèe, woweèe a ker kaashi map mmir, buwa'laèr woweèe a ba yá buu neè map mmir, yu' buu neè wap btuè', beèeñger, vúè aè mbeèp yaè, tá m gee woweèe a luêñ.”’
English: For this people's heart has grown callous. Their ears are dull of hearing. Their eyes they have closed. Lest they should see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and would turn again, and I would heal them.'

Limbum: Baná m ce koèñ máná weèe riñ ená nsuñ Nyúè ce kuu rluèñ aè duè neè beèe enje jáá. Woweèe a be yu'shi boèñboñ.”
English: Be it known therefore to you, that the salvation of God is sent to the nations. They will also listen.

Limbum: Pol aè ka' laèa wa'a, Jus a natïì a duê, a ce sár mnsár a waâp mú tatap seê.
English: When he had said these words, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.

Limbum: Pol aè m cu mbe ndaèp aè bfeâ' bbaa a ce laè' ndap anaè. E m ce koni beèe wááwá ce a m ce vúè aè ryá ye.
English: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house, and received all who were coming to him,

Limbum: E m ce feè'shi aèmboè kúú Nyúè, a ce yá'ni beèe buu kuu Tata Jisos Kraêis. E m geèe wa'a neè ñger-ñwáè, ñwáè aè ce jepsi ye ka'.
English: preaching the Kingdom of God, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.

Limbum: Ñwaè' ca ce sañ máâ Pol ce m yu ñwáè rfaè' neè Jisos Kraêis. Nyúè aè m ce máè ená m ba ñwáè ntuu neè Jisoès, a fúr máè ená m fe'shi yïì Nsuñ Mboèñmboñ neè beèe.
English: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the Good News of God,

Limbum: Nsuñ mboèñmboñ ca yu nsuñ ce Nyúè aè m kaè' neè beèe. E m laèa, ñgaâa ncep ntuu Nyúè a sañ mbe Ñwaâ' Nyúè ce yi yu rara.
English: which he promised before through his prophets in the holy Scriptures,

Limbum: Nsuñ mboèñmboñ ca kuèu muu yïì ce Jisos Kraâis ce e yu Tata neè seèe. AÈ ka' ba aèmboè li rbi, a m bi ye mbe ndúè' Dávïìd.
English: concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh,

Limbum: AÈ ka' ba yi aèmboè yi yú' ce yi yu rara, Tata Nyúè aè fúr Jisoès efa rkwe a yeâ ñger, aè rduèñshi ená e yu muu yïì.
English: who was declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,

Limbum: Yu njo' Jisoès ce Nyúè aè túr máè aè ntee boèñboñ, a fa máè fáñ aè rba ñwáè ntuu, tá beâe aè bto' wááwá a bo byemi neè ye, yu'ni neè ye, naèa ye mbekïì.
English: through whom we received grace and apostleship, for obedience of faith among all the nations, for his name's sake;

Limbum: Wee weèe yu aè múè beèe ce Nyúè aè ce ená a ba beèe Jisos Kraêis.
English: among whom you are also called to belong to Jesus Christ;

Limbum: M ce sañ ñwaè' ca neè weèe wááwá ce weèe yu aè rla' Ruêm, ce Nyúè aè koèñ weèe, a ká' weèe ená weèe ba yïì beèe. M ce loo máná Nyúè ce e yu yïìseèe Ta ker ba Tata Jisos Kraâis túr weèe aè ntee boèñboñ ker fa weèe cumúnyañ.
English: to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

Limbum: Tá m ka' laèa buu moè', m ce yoèñshi yaè Nyúè aè rlii Jisos Kraâis njo' weèe wááwá, njobeè' beèe a ce suñ aèmboè le rbyemïì aè bdïì' wááwá.
English: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.

Limbum: Nyúè ce m ce faè' neè ye neè ya ntee wááwá aèmboè m ce feè'shi Nsuñ Mboèñmboñ aèmboè muu yïì na, rïìñ ená m ce loo neè weèe aè nfeè' wááwá.
English: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Good News of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you always in my prayers,

Limbum: M ce loo máná Nyúè aè ka' byemi, e fa máè fáñ seè'ni tá m vú yá weèe.
English: requesting, if by any means now at last I may be prospered by the will of God to come to you.

Limbum: M ce koèñ aè ryá weèe seê, tá m bo koni bghoènïì ce aè yú', táá tatap.
English: For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end that you may be established;

Limbum: Yi yu ená seèe ja' viseèe mnyor. M be túr ñger njo' le rbyemïì tá weèe túr ñger njo' la rbyemïì.
English: that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other's faith, both yours and mine.

Limbum: Bfúr waê, m ce koèñ máná weèe riñ ená yu nfeè' magoèr ce má ke loè kwa'shi ená m vú yá weèe. caar ba' ntïìni na, máâ kwaè'shi wa'a, yuu mo' yi ku jepsi máè. M ce koèñ aè rgeèe tá beèe a byemi neè Jisoès tá la rfaè' li ba neè sá'-ñwáè a weâe mú aèmboè li yu neè beèe enje jáá foñ naè.
English: Now I don't desire to have you unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you, and was hindered so far, that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among the rest of the Gentiles.

Limbum: Yu ya dïì' ená m fe'shi Nsuñ Mboèñmboñ neè beèe wááwá; m be feè'shi neè beèe Greêk, ba neè beèe ce a yu beèe Greâk ka', ker ba neè beèe ce a rïìñ ñwaè' ba beèe ce a rïìñ ñwaè' ka'.
English: I am debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish.

Limbum: A mbuèu ce máè láè ntee aè rfeè'shi Nsuñ Mboèñmboñ neè weèe ce weèe yu aè rla' Rum foñ.
English: So, as much as is in me, I am eager to preach the Good News to you also who are in Rome.

Limbum: Rïìtu yi ce koo máè neè Nsuñ Mboèñmboñ ca ka'. Nsuñ Mboèñmboñ ca yu ñger Nyúè ce yi geèe beèe ce a byemi a luêñ. Ca yi yu entombïì neè Juês, a ka' ba foñ neè beèe enje jáá.
English: For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, for it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes; for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.

Limbum: Nsuñ Mboèñmboñ ca ce duèñshi seèe njáèá njïì ce Nyúè e ke geèe beèe a ba byáánïì a yeâ bsii. Njáèá njïì anaè aè káè' neè rbyemïì, a misi neè rbyemïì. Yi ku ba aèmboè a sañ mbe Ñwaâ' Nyúè enáê, “Ñwáè ce e yu yáánïì aè bsii Nyúè njobeè' e byemi neè ye, ñgaèñ be luèñ.”
English: For in it is revealed God's righteousness from faith to faith. As it is written, But the righteous shall live by faith.

Limbum: Nyúè ce ko'si rshentee neè beèe ce a geèe buu bbebep neè ye, a ker ce geèe neè bee moè' foñ naè. Yaèp buu bbebep anaè ce jepsi beèe efa rrïìñ yuu mini.
English: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,

Limbum: Nyúè ce ko'si li rshentee njobeè' buu wááwá ce aède' beèe a riñ aèmboè ye vi yu brara neè woweèe. Nyúè ye ye aè duèñshi woweèe buu anaè.
English: because that which is known of God is revealed in them, for God revealed it to them.

Limbum: Káâ' aè nfeè' ce Nyúè aè m geèe ñgoèñ, buu ce Nyúè aè m geèe vi ce duèñshi beèe buu ce aède' woweèe a m ba riñ kuu ye ka' naè. Vi ce duèñshi boèñboñ seê, ená e túr ñger ce aède' yi ke mi ka', a ker ce duèñshi foñ ená e yu Nyúè. Baná njïì moè' yu aègho ce aède' woweèe a fúr yap tu ka'.
English: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity; that they may be without excuse.

Limbum: Ka' woweèe a rïìñ Nyúè wa'a, woweèe a ce kuè'si ye ka', a ker ce yoèñshi ye ka'. Yi ka' ba wa'a, bfee vi jep woweèe, woweèe a riñ yuu ka'.
English: Because, knowing God, they didn't glorify him as God, neither gave thanks, but became vain in their reasoning, and their senseless heart was darkened.

Limbum: Woweèe a m ce laèa ená woweèe a túr bfee, a kúti ba blúr.
English: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

Limbum: Woweèe a m borni efa rloo neè Nyúè ce e yu ñwáè foèo a ker ba Nyúè ce e ke kwe ka', a ce loo ba neè blañ ce a soèp vi feeseè ñwáè ce e ke loè ku kwe, ba bsiñ ba mnyaèa ker ba buu ce vi túr mnyoâr ka'.
English: and traded the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, and four-footed animals, and creeping things.

Limbum: A mbuèu ce Nyúè aè maè'shi ená woweèe a gee buu bbebep aèmboè woweèe a ce koèñ aè rgeèe. Woweèe a ce geèe buu ce vi yu neè rïìtu-ñwáè neè wap mnyor, a waâp mú.
English: Therefore God also gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonored among themselves,

Limbum: Woweèe a maè' mini Nyúè, a lor ba mnde'. Woweèe a ce loo ba neè buu ce Nyúè aè m geèe, a ce faè' ba neè buu anaè, a ke' ce loo neè Nyúè ce e m geèe buu anaè ka'. Yu ye ce beèe a ba ce yoèñshi aè nfeè' wááwá. Yi yu wa'a.
English: who exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.

Limbum: Yi ka' ba wa'a, Nyúè aè ma'shïì ená woweèe a gee buu ce a ce koèñ aè rgeèe, aè ba buu ce vi yu neè rïìtu-ñwáè. Bbyeèñge a kupse yuu ce ñwáè aè ba geèe, a ce geèe ba yuu ce ñwáè aè ba geèe ka'.
English: For this reason, God gave them up to vile passions. For their women changed the natural function into that which is against nature.

Limbum: Mmbañruè wowo a bornïì efa rnoèñ a bbyeèñge weèe, a ce luèu aè rnoèñ ba a mmbañruè mo' weèe, a ce geèe buu ce vi yu neè rïìtu-ñwáè seê. Woweèe a ká' ñgá' mbe waâp nduè, aè ba ñgá' ce e ghááte aè yaèp buu bbebep anaè.
English: Likewise also the men, leaving the natural function of the woman, burned in their lust toward one another, men doing what is inappropriate with men, and receiving in themselves the due penalty of their error.

Limbum: AÈ ka' ba njobeè' beèe ca a kani efa rrïìñ Nyúè aèmboè yaèp Nyúè, Nyúè aè ma'shïì woweèe a ce kwaè'shi ba mkwaè'shïû mmbembep tá woweèe a bo geèe buu ce vi yu yáánïì ka' na.
English: Even as they refused to have God in their knowledge, God gave them up to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not fitting;

Limbum: Yap ntee yi ruu neè buu bbebep njáèá jáá jáèá jáá. Woweèe a ce geèe bsaèrbuu. Woweèe a lá mmir mbenduè buu beèe mo', a ce kwaè'shi bebep aèmboè beèe mo'. Woweèe a ce ko'ndoñ, a ce yúshi beèe, a ce reè bkoèr a beèe weèe, a ce bo' beèe, a túr mntee byayañ neè beèe, a ce cúè beèe, a ce sa' beèe.
English: being filled with all unrighteousness, sexual immorality, wickedness, covetousness, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil habits, secret slanderers,

Limbum: Woweèe a baèa Nyúè, a ce nyúè' beèe, a ce naèa tu, a ce yu' nyor, a ce kwaè'shi mnduunjïì jáá jáèá jáá ce aède' woweèe a gee buu bbebep. Woweèe a ce yu'ni neè wap mma ba wap bta ka'.
English: backbiters, hateful to God, insolent, haughty, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

Limbum: Woweèe a rïìñ yuu ka'. Woweèe a kaè' yuu, gee yuu anaè ka', a ce koèñ beèe ka', a ce koosimnse neè beèe ka'.
English: without understanding, covenant breakers, without natural affection, unforgiving, unmerciful;

Limbum: Woweèe a rïìñ ená Nyúè ce laèa ená beèe ce a ce geèe njáèá buu ca a ghááte aè rkweñgeèr. Ka' woweèe a rïìñ wa'a, woweèe a ku ce geèe yap yu buu ca. Yuu ce yi bep seê, yi yu ená woweèe a ce laèa ená beèe ce a ce geèe njáèá buu ca a geèe yáánïì.
English: who, knowing the ordinance of God, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but also approve of those who practice them.

Limbum: Baná wáâ ñwáè ce aè ce sa' beèe mo', mboè wáè rïìñ wáná aède' aè fúr yo tu efa mnsa' Nyúè ka' a? Wáè ka' laèa ená woweèe a geèe buu bbebep, baná wáè ce sa' yoè nyor foñ njobeè' wáè ku ce geèe ba njáèá buu ce woweèe a ce geèe.
English: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, whoever you are who judge. For in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself. For you who judge practice the same things.

Limbum: Seèe rïìñ seená Nyúè e ke geèe yáánïì aè nfeè' ce e ce sa' beèe ce a ce geèe njáèá buu ca.
English: We know that the judgment of God is according to truth against those who practice such things.

Limbum: Ñkaraè, waè' wáè ka' ce sa' beèe ce a ce geèe njáèá buu ca, ker ce geèe vi foñ, waè' aède' Nyúè buu efa rsa' wáè a?
English: Do you think this, O man who judges those who practice such things, and do the same, that you will escape the judgment of God?

Limbum: Waè' aè ce loèr ñgeâe boèñboñ ce Nyúè ce geèe neè beèe, a gee yuu mo' neè woweèe ka', a túr ntee múfáèá naè, aè yuu cicïì a? Mboè wáè rïìñ wáná Nyúè ce geèe ñgeâe boèñboñ ca neè wáè wa'a, a ce fa wáè fáñ tá aè bo kupse yo ñgeâe bebep a?
English: Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, forbearance, and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?

Limbum: Wáè teèe tu, a kani efa rkupseè, baná aè ce keè' seè'ni ba rshentee Nyúè ce li be keè yááti aèwañ aè noèñ ce e be keè sa' beèe wááwá aè njïû yáánïì naè.
English: But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart you are treasuring up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath, revelation, and of the righteous judgment of God;

Limbum: Nyúè be keè laè' ñwáè wááwá aè buu wááwá ce ñgaèñ aè m geèe.
English: who will pay back to everyone according to their works:

Limbum: Beèe ce a láè ntee aè rgeèe buu bboèñboñ aè nfeè' wááwá, a lá mmir mbenduè bkuè' ese Nyúè ba ryu'nïì ba ryoèñ ce nfeseè, Nyúè be geèe tá woweèe a cu nfeseè.
English: to those who by patience in well-doing seek for glory, honor, and incorruptibility, eternal life;

Limbum: Beèe moè' ce a yu bwer, a kani yuu mini, a ce geèe ba buu bbebep naè, a be yá ñgá' rshentee ba bepntee Nyúè.
English: but to those who are self-seeking, and don't obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, will be wrath and indignation,

Limbum: E be keè fa ñgá' neè ñwáè wááwá ce e ce geèe buu bbebep tá woweèe a yu' ryañ seê. E be keè káè' neè Juês, ka' du mbenduè beèe enje jáá foñ.
English: oppression and anguish, on every soul of man who works evil, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

Limbum: AÈ ka' ba yi aèmboè beèe ce a ce geèe buu bboèñboñ, woweèe a be keè koni bkuè' ba ryu'nïì ba cumúnyañ ese Nyúè. E be keè káè' neè Juês, ka' fa neè beèe enje jáá foñ.
English: But glory, honor, and peace go to every man who works good, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

Limbum: Nyúè e ke so'niñgoèñ ka'.
English: For there is no partiality with God.

Limbum: Beèe ce a geèe buu bbebep, a riñ mncir Nyúè ka', a be bú, ka' a be keè sa' woweèe neè mncir ka' wa'a. Beèe ce a geèe buu bbebep a riñ mncir Nyúè naè, Nyúè be sa' woweèe neè mncir anaè.
English: For as many as have sinned without law will also perish without the law. As many as have sinned under the law will be judged by the law.

Limbum: Beèe ce Nyúè aè geèe woweèe a ba byáánïì a yeâ bsii yu beèe ce a ce yu' mncir ba neè btuè' caè'caè' ka', yu beèe ce a ce láè mncir.
English: For it isn't the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be justified

Limbum: Beèe ce a yu Jus ka', a riñ mncir ka', a ka' ce geèe buu mo' ce mncir vi ce laèa aè mkwaè'shïì map, ka' woweèe a rïìñ mncir ka' wa'a, woweèe a ku riñ yuu ce yi yu yáánïì.
English: for when Gentiles who don't have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves,

Limbum: Yap ñgeèe yi ce duèñshi ená mncir Nyúè anaè vi yu njep waâp ntee ghup. Wap bfee vi ce geèe woweèe a riñ wa'a foñ njobeè' woweèe a geèe yuu boèñboñ, ku rïîñ, a geèe yuu bebep, ku rïîñ.
English: in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them

Limbum: A mboè yi be keè ba wa'a aè noèñ ce Nyúè be fa ñger neè Jisos Kraâis tá e sa' beèe a yeâ tuè, teni wap mnsa' naè. E be sa' woweèe aè buu wááwá ce woweèe a m ce geèe aè bsúèti aèmboè m ce feè'shi Nsuñ Mboèñmboñ, a ce suñ beèe naè.
English: in the day when God will judge the secrets of men, according to my Good News, by Jesus Christ.

Limbum: Wáè ce aè ce naèa nyor ená a wáè ñwáè Juês, aè ce laèa ená aè yu yáánïì njobeè' aè rïìñ mncir, a ce naèa nyor ená aè rïìñ Nyúè jáá,
English: Indeed you bear the name of a Jew, and rest on the law, and glory in God,

Limbum: wáè rïìñ yuu ce Nyúè ce koèñ, a riñ yuu ce yi yu boèñboñ njobeè' a yá'ni wáè mncir Nyúè.
English: and know his will, and approve the things that are excellent, being instructed out of the law,

Limbum: Wáè loèr yo yu ená aède' aè duñshïì mnfeèp nduunjïì. AÈ ce laèa wáná aè yu rraa neè beèe ce a yu aè túè'nji.
English: and are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light to those who are in darkness,

Limbum: AÈ ce laèa wáná aède' aè yá'ni blúr, ker yá'ni foñ beèe ce a rïìñ buu ka', njobeè' mncir vi fa wáè bfee, a gee wáè riñ yuu mini.
English: a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of babies, having in the law the form of knowledge and of the truth.

Limbum: Waè' wáè ce wáâ ke yá'ni beèe mo', wáè yá'ni yoè nyor a? Wáè ce wáâ ke yá'ni ená beèe a fa yáèá ka', waè' wáâ ke yáèá a?
English: You therefore who teach another, don't you teach yourself? You who preach that a man shouldn't steal, do you steal?

Limbum: Wáè ce aè ce laèa ená beèe a fa koo bbyeèñge beèe mo' ka', waè' wáâ ke koo bbyeèñge beèe mo' a? Wáè ce aè baèa mnyúè enjep ñgoèñ na, waè' wáâ ke yáèá buu embe ndap mnyúè anaè a?
English: You who say a man shouldn't commit adultery. Do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?

Limbum: Wáè ce aè ce naèa nyor ená aè riñ mncir Nyúè seê, waè' wáâ ke geèe beèe a ce laèa bebep aèmboè Nyúè njobeè' aè ce bú' mncir anaè a?
English: You who glory in the law, through your disobedience of the law do you dishonor God?

Limbum: A sañ mbe Ñwaâ' Nyúè enáê, “Beèe enje jáá a ce bepsi rlii Nyúè njobeè' yuu ce weèe ce geèe.”
English: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, just as it is written.

Limbum: AÈ ce geèe búè aè rduèñshi ená aè yu ñwáè Nyúè. Búè ce aè ce geèe anaè be ba neè sá'-ñwáè, ce aè ka' ce láè mncir Nyúè. Wáè ka' ce bú' mncir Nyúè, baná yi yu seè'ni aèmboè wáè geèe lá búè ka' wa'a.
English: For circumcision indeed profits, if you are a doer of the law, but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.

Limbum: AÈ ka' ba yi aèmboè ñwáè ce e geèe búè ka', ñgaèñ aè ka' ce láè mncir Nyúè, baná Nyúè be kuè loèr ñgaèñ aèmbo ñwáè ce e geèe búè wáá wa'a.
English: If therefore the uncircumcised keep the ordinances of the law, won't his uncircumcision be accounted as circumcision?

Limbum: Ñwáè ca be coosi wáè ce wáè geèe búè, a riñ mncir Nyúè ce a sañ mbe Ñwaâ' Nyúè, a lá vi ka' naè.
English: Won't the uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfills the law, judge you, who with the letter and circumcision are a transgressor of the law?

Limbum: Yi yu ená ñwáè ce e yu ñwáè Jus ghup yu ba ñwáè ce a ce yá ba neè mmir ka'. Búè ce yu búè mini aè bsii Nyúè yu ba yïì ce aè geèe ñwáè ka'.
English: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh;
